caption: The drawing features two carved, wooden blocks depicted against a light tan background. Both objects are mostly brown with darker shading to indicate depth and texture. Each block is square-faced and features a symmetrical, geometric floral pattern carved into the top and one visible side. The design consists of four petal-like shapes radiating from the center, surrounded by a border of small triangles. The top block is shown from a top-down perspective, while the lower block is shown from an angle, revealing both the front and side with the same carved design. The blocks have visible carved edges and are rendered to show the three-dimensional aspects. To the left of the lower block, there is text in grayish-blue reading “MENNYZYWYSEN.” The overall composition is simple, with the objects centered and separated, and there is minimal background detail.
title: Pa. German Butter Mold
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
